title: Hurricane Florence Relief Efforts
description: Cpl. Jeron Blackmon, assistant mission commander with CLB-8 and Zachary Hierl, a paramedic with Onslow County EMS and a member of Onslow County Swift Fire rescue team, provide an interview regarding recovery efforts in Jacksonville, N.C., Sept. 16, 2018. Marines from across II Marine Expeditionary Force and Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune are assisting with disaster relief efforts for those affected by strong winds, heavy rain, power outages, and flooded housing due to Hurricane Florence. Hurricane Florence, with its heavy rain and strong winds, is the biggest storm to hit the Carolinas since Hurricane Floyd in 1999, causing power outages and flooding damages and forcing many first responders to be ready at a moment's notice. (U.S. Marine Corps video by Staff Sgt. Omar Elorza)

transcript.text: In the wake of Hurricane Florence, we have been responding to multiple calls for
swift water rescues as well as people trapped in their homes needing assistance
and being evacuated. And we're working to get them out. Some homes are very flooded,
some homes they're just stranded they have nowhere to go so we have to bring
them to a shelter. Joint efforts with the Marines has been absolutely phenomenal.
Having that great relationship with the base and the county is beneficial to
all the citizens in Oslo County. I'm proud to call myself Marine because I'm
able to help them out in town. Being able to team up together to get out and
help those in need has been absolutely awesome. I think it's been amazing the
trucks have been a huge help to access places that we couldn't access before.
We would not have been able to facilitate that so without the help of the Marine Corps.
